Save states have a container version and separate subsystem chunk versions;
these numbers are distinct from the Copperline release version.
Flat states from Copperline 0.19 and earlier (container 1-80)
Refused; boot the guest again and create a new state.
Accepted without the later thumbnail/metadata card.
Current container. Required chunks and their versions still need to be supported by the reader.
Upgraded only when a migration exists. A missing migration fails with the chunk name and versions.
Refused. Use the build that wrote it or a compatible newer build.

For example, 1.1.0 reads old CIA version-1 chunks by migration and writes
CIA version 2. That does not make the resulting states readable by 1.0.x.
Forward compatibility is not guaranteed merely because the container version
is the same. Preserve a copy before trying a state in another build.

1.2.0 is another one-way boundary even though the container and chunk
versions did not change: 1.2.0 reads 1.1.0 states, but 1.1.0 cannot read
1.2.0 states. Its decoder requires the floppy drives’

and
the device clock’s wall-clock fields, which newer states no longer write. An
error naming one of those missing fields calls for a newer reader or a new
snapshot made by the older executable.

Built-in board drivers that run from a ROM inside Copperline are not stored
in a state. 1.2.0 changed the

driver, so a 1.1.0 state
saved with a

drive attached can hang after loading in 1.2.0;
boot that machine afresh and save a new state.

The reader must also have support for every expansion board in the state.

These limits describe hardware behaviour, rather than a compatibility promise
for individual programs. The linked subsystem chapters give the details.
The later CPUs do not have a complete pipeline/overlap timing model. Instruction correctness and measured bus timing do not imply cycle-exact accelerator execution.
also adapts the CPU clock to spare host time. Use the default fixed clock and JIT disabled for precise timing investigations.
Not modelled. The on-chip MMUs on the full 68030/040/060 are separate supported devices; EC variants omit them.
Generic physical genlock video input/output and ZD key-signal output beyond register storage are not emulated. External genlock sync (
), the Video Toaster 4000 video-slot card, and the CD32 FMV module’s internal digital video compositing are separate supported features.
Sub-unit DDF stop effects beyond whole fetch-unit completion are not modelled.
Subcode R-W data reaches the CDTV and CD32 only from an image that stored it: a
file beside the image, a cue sheet
track, or a CHD with raw subcode. CHD “cooked” subcode is not read.
The capture FIFO is a stub: reads return zero and no record half-full interrupt fires. Playback is implemented.
Clip recording into the Flyer, SMPTE time code, and the TBC module are not emulated. Playback, editing/cutting, and clip import/export are supported.
